title: Bakery Cost Per Lead 2026: Click Prices and Ad Budgets
summary: A click for 'bakery' costs $0.53 on average on Google in the US. See cost per lead at 5% to 15% conversion, channel comparison and a monthly budget formula.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- A click on the main bakery searches costs $0.42 to $0.87 on average on Google in the US: $0.53 for 'bakery', $0.42 for 'bakery near me' and $0.87 for 'custom cakes'.
- At the $0.53 click for 'bakery', a 10% conversion rate (an example) gives $5.30 per lead, and 5% gives $10.60. For wider context, LocaliQ's 2026 Google search figure for restaurants and food is $30.57 per lead.
- LocaliQ's 2026 all-industry figures are $27.39 per Meta lead and $66.69 per Google search lead. Those are not bakery numbers, but they show Meta leads cost less on paper and come from people who were not searching.
- A sensible starting budget: orders you want, divided by the share of leads that order, times your cost per lead.


## What a click costs


Bakery clicks are cheap next to most local trades. Here is what a click costs on Google in the US for the three searches most bakeries care about.


Search Searches a month (US) Average click price Top-of-page range


bakery 1,500,000 $0.53 $0.41 to $3.80


bakery near me 3,350,000 $0.42 $0.36 to $2.60


custom cakes 49,500 $0.87 $0.27 to $1.61


The spread comes from three things. Urgency matters: someone who needs a cake by Saturday will pay more to be seen than someone idly browsing. Competition matters: the top-of-page range for 'bakery' runs from $0.41 to $3.80, so the high end is more than nine times the low end, and the ceiling rises where several shops and grocery chains bid on the same search. City matters too, because a dense metro with many bakeries pushes prices toward the top of each range, while a small town sits near the bottom. For more on how Google prices clicks in general, see[what Google Ads costs](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-ads-cost) .


## From click to cost per lead


A click is not a lead. Cost per lead is the click price divided by the share of clicks that become a call, a form or an order request. This table uses the $0.53 average click for 'bakery'. The last column is an example: it assumes 1 in 3 leads turns into a booked order.


Conversion rate Cost per lead Cost per booked order (example: 1 in 3 leads books)


5% $0.53 / 0.05 = $10.60, about $11 $10.60 x 3 = $31.80, about $32


10% $0.53 / 0.10 = $5.30, about $5 $5.30 x 3 = $15.90, about $16


15% $0.53 / 0.15 = $3.53, about $4 $3.53 x 3 = $10.60, about $11


Your conversion rate does most of the work. A clear page with a menu, photos and a tap-to-call button sits at the better end of this table, and a vague page sits at the worse end. To try your own click price, conversion rate and booking rate, use the[cost per lead calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cost-per-lead-calculator) .


## Google Ads vs Local Services Ads vs Facebook for bakeries


Google Ads (Search) Local Services Ads Facebook and Instagram (Meta)


How you pay Per click, set by auction Per lead, with the price set by Google by category and area Per impression or click, or per lead on a lead form


What intent High: the person typed 'bakery near me' or 'custom cakes' High, but only where Google offers your category Lower: the person was scrolling, not searching


When it wins for a bakery Walk-in traffic, custom cake and event orders from people ready to buy Bakeries are not a typical category, so for most it is not available. Check your account before planning around it Holiday preorders, seasonal boxes, cake showcases and offers that look good in a photo


Local Services Ads are built for trades such as plumbers and locksmiths, where a customer wants a vetted pro to call. If you want to see how the program works, read our guide to[Google Local Services Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) . For a bakery, your Google Business Profile and Search ads usually cover the same ground.


These are the benchmark cost per lead figures from LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks. Read each one for the industry it covers:


- **Google search, restaurants and food:** $30.57 per lead, with an average click of $2.05 and a 8.05% conversion rate.
- **Google search, all industries:** $66.69 per lead.
- **Meta lead ads, all industries:** $27.39 per lead.


The restaurants and food figures are a wider category than bakeries, and the bakery click prices above are lower than that $2.05 average. Treat the benchmarks as a ceiling for sanity checks, not a forecast. For more categories, see[average cost per lead by industry](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry) .


## How much to spend each month


Start from the orders you want, not from a round number.


**Monthly budget = (orders wanted / share of leads that order) x cost per lead**


A worked example, with every input stated:


1. You want 20 extra orders a month.
2. Say 1 in 3 leads orders. That means you need 20 x 3 = 60 leads.
3. Say your click is $0.53 and 5% of clicks become leads. Cost per lead is $0.53 / 0.05 = $10.60.
4. Budget: 60 x $10.60 = $636 a month, which is 1,200 clicks at $0.53.


If you target 'custom cakes' instead, the click is $0.87, so the cost per lead at 5% is $17.40 and the same 60 leads cost $1,044. Start on one channel, usually Google Search, run it long enough to see a steady cost per lead, then add Meta once you know your numbers. Our[bakery advertising guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/bakery-advertising) covers the wider plan.


## How to lower your cost per lead


- **Make one clear offer.** A free tasting for wedding cakes, a preorder deadline for holiday boxes or a dozen-pack price gives people a reason to act now. To see what works, see what bakeries run on Facebook in the[bakery ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/bakery-ads) .
- **Send clicks to a focused page.** Show real photos, prices or a starting price, pickup times and one order button. Do not send people to a home page full of other things.
- **Answer every call and message.** A cake customer who gets voicemail on a busy morning orders from the next bakery. Use a text-back or a voicemail that links to your order form.
- **Add negative keywords.** Block searches such as 'recipe', 'bakery jobs', 'baking class' and 'bakery equipment' so you do not pay for clicks from people who will never order.
- **Set your service area to match pickup and delivery.** Do not pay for clicks from people outside the distance you will drive or who will not travel to your counter.
- **Keep the lead form short.** Ask for the date needed, number of servings, pickup or delivery and a phone number. Extra fields cut the number of leads, and a short form gets you more orders to quote on.
